newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-SAKU MAY PRODUCE SOME BEER IN LATVIA.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-SAKU MAY PRODUCE SOME BEER IN LATVIA.

text.p: Estonia's largest beer producer Saku said on Monday it was considering moving a part of its beer production to Latvia after a recent government excise rise.
"We are considering different measures in response to the new excise law," Saku public relations department head Anu Oun told Reuters.
Saku is owned by Baltic Beverages, a venture between Hartwall and Pripps Ringnes, part of Norway's Orkla.
"We wish to keep our market share and it is possible that some production could be moved to Latvia or Lithuania but most likely to Latvia," she said.
The new law, in force from July 1, imposes a higher excise duty rate on firms making more than 20 million litres of beer a year and on foreign imports.
Oun said that the company in 1997 expected to make around the same level of beer as last year, some 26 million litres.
The move could involve the production of some 19.99 million litres in Estonia and another six million litres elsewhere. Only the six million litres would then attract the higher tax rate.
However, Saku has not yet made a final decision on how to work around the new law, she said.
"We must review our business strategy and consider what options we have. A decision should be made in May," Oun added.
